compiled_state.description:
## Impact, stated first

`rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts` — the paging alarm that bug [rebar:34cd-1a7c-b9b1-4b05] created specifically so the LLM-Review live-lock could never again be invisible — **fired three times in the last seven days**, most recently **2026-08-11T20:05 PDT**, i.e. during the current landing burst. Each firing means an in-flight LLM-Review was killed by a container recreation.

By 34cd design that is the alarm doing its job. The reason it is worth a ticket is that **firing is supposed to be the exceptional case**, reachable (per 34cd) only by "a chronically busy bot" — and three firings in a week says the exceptional case is now routine.

Found by an automated ops error sweep of AWS CloudWatch (account 896586841071, us-east-1) over 2026-08-05T00:00Z -> 2026-08-12T04:00Z. No open ticket covers this; 34cd is closed, and [rebar:9ec0-02b2-8494-4ea5] (in_progress) covers only the *shutdown-side* half — manual restart, reboot, autodeploy rollback — which is a different trigger from the one seen here.

## Occurrences (rebar/host:review_interrupts, Sum > 0)

- 2026-08-07 04:33 PDT
- 2026-08-07 05:55 PDT
- 2026-08-11 20:05 PDT

Alarm state history confirms each as a full OK -> ALARM -> OK episode, self-clearing in ~15 minutes.

## The deferral run-up is the interesting part

`rebar/host:deploy_deferrals` immediately before the 2026-08-11 interrupt:

    2026-08-11 19:00 PDT   11 deferrals
    2026-08-11 20:00 PDT    3 deferrals
    2026-08-11 20:05 PDT    -> review_interrupts = 1

The autodeploy tick is ~2 minutes, so 11 deferrals in the 19:00 hour is roughly 22 minutes of continuous deferring, continuing into the next hour until the interrupt lands. `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` is **1800s (30 min)**. The run-up therefore matches the **`bound-exceeded`** path: the bot stayed busy long enough to spend the entire bound, after which autodeploy proceeds and kills the review. The 2026-08-07 firings show the same shape (13 deferrals at 04:00 -> interrupt 04:33; 15 deferrals at 05:00 -> interrupt 05:55).

## Stated uncertainty — this is an inference, not a reading

`rebar/host:review_interrupts` is published with **no dimensions**, so the metric cannot distinguish the two reasons the marker is emitted: `bound-exceeded` (chronically busy) versus `signal-unavailable` (the `/health` `in_flight` signal was unreadable and the deploy proceeded blind). The deferral run-up above is strong circumstantial evidence for `bound-exceeded`, but **confirming it requires `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy` on the box**, which this sweep did not have access to. That check should be step one.

The distinction matters a great deal, because the two readings imply opposite fixes: `bound-exceeded` means reviews are queueing faster than they complete and the bound is correctly bounding a real overload; `signal-unavailable` means the drain check itself is broken and **every** deploy has been running blind — which would be a silent regression of 34cd rather than its intended behavior.

## Why not just raise DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX

Recording this so it is not the reflexive first move: 34cd chose 1800s deliberately as 1.5x the app-side `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (1200s) ceiling, with a test asserting `bound >= REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to keep the two in lockstep. Raising it would trade a killed review for a longer deploy stall, and if the true cause is `signal-unavailable` the bound is not involved at all and raising it would change nothing while appearing to.

## Secondary observation, same hour

`rebar/host:mirror_out_of_sync` also recorded a datapoint at 2026-08-11 20:00 PDT (and on 08-04, 08-05, 08-07 x2). These are isolated single datapoints that never breached `rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync`, so no alarm fired — consistent with brief Gerrit->GitHub replication lag rather than a stuck mirror. Noted for correlation only; not claimed as related.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The reason field behind each of the three firings is read from `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy` and recorded here: `bound-exceeded` or `signal-unavailable`.
- [ ] If `signal-unavailable`: the `/health` `in_flight` probe is repaired, since that state means 34cd`s drain check has been inert.
- [ ] If `bound-exceeded`: a decision is recorded on whether a landing burst that outlasts a 30-minute bound is acceptable steady state, given that each firing kills a review the reconciler must then retry.
- [ ] `rebar/host:review_interrupts` carries enough dimensionality (or a companion metric) that a future sweep can tell the two reasons apart **without** shell access to the host — the absence of that is why this ticket has to hedge.

## Notes

Filed by an automated ops error sweep. No code was changed and nothing was mutated in AWS (read-only calls only). No file_impact is recorded — the correct target depends on which reason the journald check returns.
compiled_state.title: The autodeploy review-interrupt alarm has fired 3 times in 7 days post-34cd: the deferral bound is being SPENT during landing bursts, not merely approached
